item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
506
ABPZ20 KNHC 262342
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll, and
on Tropical Storm Iselle, located well to the west of the southern
tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific (EP93):
A broad area of low pressure located well south of southwestern
Mexico continues to produce a large area of showers and
thunderstorms. Although the system has not become better organized
over the last several hours, environmental conditions are still
expected to support gradual development of this system, and a
tropical depression is likely to form tonight or on Thursday. The
system is forecast to move west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well
offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
An area of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands has become slightly better organized over the last
several hours. Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression is likely to
form late this week or early this weekend while the system drifts to
the northeast, before turning westward by early next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form this weekend well to the
south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear
favorable for some gradual development of this system, and a
tropical depression is likely to form early next week while it moves
westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves
slowly west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Zelinsky

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 270232
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...ISELLE HAS BECOME A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE...
...THIS IS THE FINAL NHC ADVISORY ON THE SYSTEM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.0N 125.9W
ABOUT 1015 MI...1635 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle
was located near latitude 23.0 North, longitude 125.9 West. The
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph
(15 km/h) and this motion is expected to continue over the next few 
days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Iselle has become a Post-Tropical Cyclone and is expected to 
continue to weaken until it dissipates in a couple of days or less. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle will continue to affect the west
coast of the Baja California Peninsula for a couple more days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system. For additional information on the remnant low 
please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and 
on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Hagen/Papin

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 270233
TCDEP4
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Wed Aug 26 2026

Iselle continues to have no deep convective organization this 
evening with the low-level center still fully exposed due to dry air 
and moderate wind shear. With the lack of convection occuring, 
Iselle is now considered to have become a Post-Tropical Cyclone. The 
most recent TAFB Dvorak fix has 1.5/25 kt and the objective 
satellite intensity estimates are in the range of 25-43 kt. Based on 
that data, the current NHC initial intensity has been set to 30 kt.

Iselle should continue to move west-northwestward over the next 
couple of days, steered by a mid-level ridge to the north of the 
cyclone. Increasing wind shear, cooler sea surface temperatures, and 
a drier air mass will continue to weaken the system. The 
post-tropical remnant low is expected to gradually spin down 
and open into a trough in about 2 to 3 days. However, it still 
remains possible that the cyclone could spin down even sooner. Very 
minor adjustments were made to the previous NHC track and intensity 
forecasts.

For additional information on the remnant low please see High Seas
Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS
header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
